record.original_question: Prove or refute the conjectured upper bound SW(1324) < e*pi*sqrt(2/3) for the Stanley-Wilf limit of the classical pattern 1324.

evidence.quote: In [23] it is conjectured that SW(1324) < eπ√2/3 ≈ 13.001954.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, viewed as the set of permutations written in one-line notation. A permutation $\pi\in S_n$ is said to contain the pattern $1324$ if there exist indices $1\le i_1<i_2<i_3<i_4\le n$ such that
$$\pi(i_1)<\pi(i_3)<\pi(i_2)<\pi(i_4).$$
Otherwise $\pi$ is said to avoid $1324$. Let $\mathrm{Av}_n(1324)$ denote the set of permutations in $S_n$ that avoid the pattern $1324$, and let $a_n=|\mathrm{Av}_n(1324)|$.

By the Marcus–Tardos theorem, the limit
$$\mathrm{SW}(1324)\;=\;\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n^{1/n}$$
exists and is finite. Prove or disprove the inequality
$$\mathrm{SW}(1324)\;<\;e^{\pi\sqrt{2/3}}\;\approx\;13.001954.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The exact value of the Stanley–Wilf limit of 1324 remains unknown. The best rigorous upper bound currently in the literature is approximately 13.5 (Bevan, Brignall, Elvey Price, Pantone, 2020), while the best lower bound is around 10.271. Since the conjectured bound $e^{\pi\sqrt{2/3}}\approx 13.0019$ lies strictly between these, the conjecture has neither been proved nor refuted.

status_evidence.title: A structural characterisation of Av(1324) and new bounds on its growth rate
status_evidence.snippet: Improved lower bound of 10.271 and upper bound of 13.5 for the growth rate of 1324-avoiding permutations.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2020 the best rigorous bounds are 10.271 < SW(1324) < 13.5, leaving the conjecture SW(1324) < e^{π√(2/3)} ≈ 13.0019 open.

status_evidence.title: Upper bounds for the Stanley-Wilf limit of 1324 and other layered patterns
status_evidence.snippet: Conditional bound SW(1324) ≤ e^{π√(2/3)} ≈ 13.001954 under an unproven monotonicity conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The bound e^{π√(2/3)} for SW(1324) is established only conditionally on a further unproved conjecture.
